condition: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (mimic of acute pancreatitis)
permutationLabel: Dangerous mimic — ruptured AAA: epigastric pain to the back, collapse, hypotension, amylase mildly raised
summary: 74-year-old hypertensive smoker with sudden epigastric pain radiating to the back and a collapse at home; BP 86/50, HR 118, pale; amylase 240 (2.4 × ULN), Hb 9.8, lactate 4.1. No imaging yet.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Sudden upper abdominal pain going through to the back, with a collapse
inputs.hpi: Sudden severe epigastric pain radiating straight through to the back 90 minutes ago, then collapsed at home and was briefly unresponsive. Now pale and sweaty. Hypertension, smoker 50 pack-years, ischaemic heart disease. Not a drinker, no gallstones known.

exam.general: Pale, clammy, alert but anxious. Pulse 118/min, BP 86/50, RR 24. Haemodynamically unstable.
exam.abdomen: Obese. Epigastric tenderness and a vague expansile fullness above the umbilicus; difficult to assess. No peritonism.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (bedside ultrasound: 7.5 cm infrarenal aneurysm with retroperitoneal haematoma). Mildly raised amylase is not pancreatitis.

mustNotMiss.note: Epigastric/back pain with collapse and hypotension in an elderly smoker is a ruptured AAA until proven otherwise; amylase can be mildly raised.

emergencyLevel.note: iOS (predicted, not observed): routine — no emergency keyword ("collapse" is not in the list).

mustExclude.note: Ruptured AAA: permissive hypotension until proximal control. A pancreatitis-style "aggressive fluid" instruction can precipitate further bleeding.
Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.

guideline.name: ESVS 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the management of abdominal aorto-iliac artery aneurysms
guideline.section: Suspected rupture: immediate vascular surgical assessment, permissive hypotension, CT angiography if stable, EVAR preferred when anatomy suitable
guideline.citation: Wanhainen A, Van Herzeele I, Bastos Goncalves F, et al. Eur J Vasc Endovasc Surg. 2024;67:192–331.

guideline.name: Revised Atlanta classification of acute pancreatitis (2012)
guideline.section: Diagnosis (2 of 3: typical pain, lipase/amylase ≥3 × ULN, imaging); severity: mild (no organ failure, no local/systemic complications), moderately severe (transient organ failure <48 h and/or local complications), severe (persistent organ failure >48 h); modified Marshall score
guideline.citation: Banks PA, Bollen TL, Dervenis C, et al. Gut. 2013;62:102–111.

rationale: Dangerous mimic for acute pancreatitis: a ruptured AAA gives epigastric pain to the back with a mildly raised amylase. Collapse, shock and a pulsatile mass must redirect the engines to an aortic emergency, and away from pancreatitis fluid protocols.

authoring.author: Claude (HPB cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations and citations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). iOS outcomes not yet observed (unverified: ios) — triage after the first CI run.
